test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following correctly characterises the regulatory and structural aspects of the NPS Vatsalya scheme, as launched in 2024?

1. The scheme is administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

2. Contributions under NPS Vatsalya are pooled into a government-managed consolidated fund without individual accounts.

3.The scheme allows a smooth shift to a regular NPS account when the subscriber turns 18 years of age.

4.Upon attaining adulthood, subscribers must compulsorily exit NPS Vatsalya and opt for the Atal Pension Yojana.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NPS Vatsalya**, launched in 2024, is a child-focused pension scheme overseen by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).
 
• Under the scheme, children below 18 years of age can have individual accounts, allowing for targeted savings with flexible contributions.
 
• Subscribers are permitted a smooth transition to a regular NPS account upon reaching 18 years of age, ensuring continuity in retirement planning.
 
• Option 3 correctly highlights that the scheme is regulated by PFRDA and facilitates the seamless migration to a standard NPS account.
 
• Contrary to some options, the scheme does not mandate a switch to Atal Pension Yojana upon adulthood but ensures voluntary transitions based on subscriber needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA):**

 
 
• PFRDA is a statutory authority under the Indian government responsible for regulating and promoting pension schemes such as the National Pension System (NPS).
 
• It plays a crucial role in ensuring the financial security of citizens post-retirement.
 
 
 
• **National Pension System (NPS):**
 
 
• NPS is a government-backed voluntary retirement savings scheme open to all Indian citizens aged 18-70.
 
• Subscribers can contribute regularly to their accounts and receive market-linked returns.
 
• NPS is managed by PFRDA and offers tax benefits under Section 80CCD(1) and 80CCD(1B).
 
 
 
• **Atal Pension Yojana (APY):**
 
 
• APY is a government-backed pension scheme focused on unorganized sector workers.
 
• It provides guaranteed pension benefits ranging from Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 per month, depending on contributions.
 
• Eligible subscribers must be between 18-40 years of age.
 
 
 
• **Child-Focused Financial Schemes:**
 
 
• Such schemes aim to inculcate early financial discipline and savings habits among children.
 
• They often include features like flexible contributions, parental oversight, and benefits tailored to future needs.
